note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God and the witness on high are not pictured, Job and his friends are shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent is shown: the tearing, striking and shooting of verses 9 to 14 are shown through a threat that has not struck yet and a target, never through wounds.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures.

sections.meaning: Long speeches that blame a suffering man only add to his misery; anyone could talk like that, but a true friend's words would strengthen him and ease his pain.

sections.meaning: His pain does not leave whether he speaks or keeps silent; he is worn out, wasted and alone, and he feels torn at, mocked and hemmed in by enemies on every side.

sections.meaning: He was living at ease when he was shattered, and now he feels set up as a target, hit again and again with no letup.

sections.meaning: He sits low in grief, his face red from weeping and the shadow of death on his eyes, yet his hands are clean of any violence and his prayer is pure.

sections.meaning: Though his friends scoff and his days are running out, he cries that his cry must not be buried, for he has a witness in heaven who will plead his case as a man pleads for his friend.

candidates.prompt: In a plain living room in soft afternoon light, a weary middle-aged man in a rumpled shirt sits slumped on the sofa with his head in one hand, eyes closed, drained and miserable. Three well-dressed visitors stand over him, all talking at him at once: one jabs a finger at him, one frowns and shakes his head, one holds a bunch of flowers while lecturing him. Their words are plainly crushing him rather than comforting him.

On the front steps of a small house on a grey, windy day, a worn-out man sits hunched with his elbows on his knees and his eyes shut. Three friends stand over him on the path, all talking at once: one wags his finger at him, one has his arms folded and shakes his head, one leans in with his mouth open mid-sentence. A gust of wind is blowing a whirl of dry leaves round them.

In a dim bathroom at night, a worn-out man who has grown very thin stands at the sink and stares into the mirror. His reflection is clearly visible and is the centre of the picture: hollow cheeks, sunken tired eyes, collarbones showing, his old shirt hanging loose on his shoulders. One small light above the mirror lights his face.

Late at night in a silent, empty house, an exhausted, thin man sits on the edge of his bed with his shoulders sagging and his hands hanging between his knees, too weary to lie down. Through the open doorway behind him the rest of the house is dark and empty: a dining table with empty chairs all round it. A single bedside lamp lights him.

In a snowy clearing at the edge of a dark winter forest, one small lone sheep stands frozen in the middle. All round it a ring of grey wolves closes in from every side, heads low, eyes fixed on it, lips drawn back from their teeth. Nothing has happened yet: the sheep is simply surrounded with no way out. Cold, clear daylight.

In a city square on a grey day, one ordinary man stands alone in the middle with his head bowed, and a crowd of people presses in round him on every side, jeering at him: mouths wide open, sneering faces, fingers pointing at him, one man leaning in close to shout in his face. No one touches him, but he is completely hemmed in.

In a quiet, peaceful green meadow full of wildflowers under a calm blue midday sky, a single round archery target stands on its wooden stand. It is riddled with arrows: dozens of arrows have struck it from every side, more arrows stand stuck in the ground round its foot, and its straw face is torn open. Nothing else is in the field.

A long stone sea wall that once sheltered a quiet garden has been broken through in gap after gap along its length. Huge grey waves pour through every breach and flood across the neat lawn and flower beds behind it. A heavy storm sky, spray flying high over the broken wall.

Portrait of an ordinary middle-aged man in a coarse, rough grey shirt, sitting on bare ground. His face is red and swollen from weeping, his eyes wet, with deep dark shadows under them. He holds both hands up open in front of his chest, palms toward the viewer, completely empty and clean. His face and his raised open hands fill the upper part of the frame. Soft, even daylight.

A man in a rough sackcloth shirt of coarse brown burlap sits in the dust of a bare, dry yard, his head bowed low, tears running down his reddened face, dust smeared on his forehead and in his hair. His hands rest open on his knees, palms up, empty and clean. Plain grey daylight.

At night a lone man stands on the bare top of a high hill under an immense, clear sky full of stars. He has lifted his face and both open arms toward the sky, calling out. He is small in the frame against the vast sky, seen from behind and a little to the side, the bright stars filling most of the picture.

On a high bare ridge on a stormy afternoon, a man stands with his tear-wet face lifted toward the sky and one hand raised, as the heavy dark clouds high above him part and a broad shaft of clear light shines down from far above. Wide view: the sky fills most of the frame and the man is small on the ridge.

In a plain modern courtroom, seen from the side, a man in an ordinary jacket stands at the table speaking earnestly toward the front of the room, one hand open as he argues his friend's case, his other hand resting firmly on the shoulder of his friend, who sits beside him worn out, head bowed and eyes wet. The front of the room is out of the frame.

On a hillside path on an overcast evening, a man stands with tears running down his face, looking up toward the sky. A few steps behind him, three of his friends stand together laughing at him, one pointing and the others shaking their heads.
